doc.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Ego, restraint and humility on the bandstand
summary: Discussing military versus individuality, he says to let others speak, not prove yourself, and not take charge of someone else's show.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: But in the military, isn’t part of their goal to make you less of an individual and more part of the group?

Less of an individual in terms of your ego. But your ego gets mellowed out to stand out among the crowd. They reward people who are better than the other. But not at the expense of the other, like musicians sometimes do. They want to be stars at my expense. And why should I allow that? Because I feel I’m just — happens all the time — it’s standard procedure in show business. “Wait a minute, I’d like to answer.” Well maybe the answer was already said. Maybe not clear enough? Maybe louder? Or how you said it. So let him have it. Don’t erase his image, his phrase. He just said it. So you don’t need to say nothing. That’s what you learn to do as commercial artists. I’ve learned it from the martial arts, this and that. That’s why you notice today I didn’t do a lot of talking. You don’t need to. The band director has it. I don’t need to prove to you I’m a general. You’ll sense it. You’ll feel it. You’ll find out. I could talk all day if I wanted to and there never is why. Half the suggestions that were made was already made by the guy conducting the band. So I don’t need to prove to him that I know. There’s a mellow way to participate with students and grown-ups alike without taking charge. Because it ain’t your show. You follow me? See you have to pick your spots. Like every time the director says something they would say, “And let me add to that.” You don’t need to add to that. That bothers me a lot.

That bothers me a lot really. I’m happy knowing what I know, who I am and what I am. I don’t need to prove it. You’ll see it, eventually, if I can do my thing, you’ll see it. I don’t have to tell anybody who I am, where I went or what I do. I can write a book. That thick. More than anybody on that bandstand. I’m telling you now because you’re interviewing me. You’d never know it.
